summary: Sonja Arntzen is a scholar of Japanology. She studied at the University of British Columbia from circa 1968 to 1979 under doctoral supervisor Leon Hurvitz (~1970–1979), and also studied under Seizan Yanagida and Sojo Hirano.

Sonya S. Lee works in Buddhist studies, sinology, and history and archaeology. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago (attested 2004) under Wu Hung, taught at Swarthmore College (2003–2004), and held a post at USC (attested 2010).

Soon-il Hwang works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed an MA at Dongguk University under Seungwon Seo and a DPhil at Mansfield College, Oxford, under Richard Gombrich, later holding a post at Dongguk University.
Soorakkulame Pemarathana is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy. He studied at the National University of Singapore under thesis supervisor Saranindranath Tagore (attested 2004).
Sophus Bugge (1833–1907) was a linguist. He studied under Albrecht Weber in 1858, taught Sten Konow, and held a post at Uppsala University.
Soshu Nishioka is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held a post as a professor at Shitennoji University, attested in 2000 and 2015.
Soshuku Shibatani works in Buddhist studies and religious studies. He studied at Waseda University and held an appointed researcher post at Koyasan University (attested 2015).

Sravana Borkataky-Varma specializes in religious studies and Indology. She has held posts at the University of North Carolina Wilmington (~2017–2020), Harvard University (~2020), and the University of Houston.

Sreeramula Rajeswara Sarma works in Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at Andhra University, Visva-Bharati University (~1957–1960), and the University of Marburg (~1964–1966, PhD), later serving as professor at Aligarh Muslim University (attested 2006–2012).

Stacey Van Vleet specializes in Tibetology, sinology, and history/archaeology. She studied at the University of Colorado Boulder (MA) and Columbia University (PhD attested 2006), where she later held a post attested in 2013.

Stanislas Julien (1797–1873) was a sinologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at the Collège de France (~1821–1832) under Jean-Pierre Abel-Rémusat, whom he succeeded in 1832, serving there as professor and administrator until 1873.
Stanley Abe specializes in history and archaeology, Buddhist studies, and sinology. He taught Jungmin Ha and held posts at Duke University (attested in 1995 and 2004).

Stanley Insler (1937–2019) was a scholar of Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Columbia College, Yale University, and the University of Tübingen, and held a long-term post at Yale University (~1964–2015).

Stanley Jeyaraja Tambiah (1929–2014) worked in religious and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Ceylon, Cornell, and Harvard. He held posts at the University of Cambridge (attested 1973) and Harvard University (~1976–2001) as Professor of Anthropology.

Stanley Weinstein (1929–2017) was a scholar of Buddhist studies, sinology, and Japanology. After studying at Harvard University (~1959–1965), he was a professor at the University of London (~1962–1968) and later served at Yale University (attested 1981–2008).

Stanley Wolpert (1927–2019) was a scholar of Indology and history/archaeology. He studied at the City College of New York (~1949–1953) and the University of Pennsylvania (~1953–1959), later serving as professor of history at UCLA (~1959–2002).
Stefan Anacker (1939–2021) was a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1964–1969) under Alex Wayman (~1965–1969).

Stefan Baums specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He completed his dissertation at the University of Washington (~2002–2009) and held posts at the University of Copenhagen (~2001–2002), Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~2011), and LMU Munich (~2011).

Stefan Larsson specializes in Tibetology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at Stockholm University (-2009) under Per-Arne Berglie and held a postdoctoral fellowship at the University of California, Berkeley (attested 2012).
Stefan Maul is a scholar of linguistics and history and archaeology. He held posts at the Free University of Berlin (1987–1995) and Heidelberg University (1995).
